# settings

<!-- Generated from the doc comments in the library. Do not edit this file. -->

The process-wide settings object.

A getter/setter pair rather than a plain field so that an invalid assignment fails at the line that made it, with the caller's stack, instead of surfacing much later as a confusing "undeclared licence" during generation.

Import from `@bonniepdf/core`.

## Properties

- [`license`](#license): Which BonniePDF licence applies to this application.

### `license`

```typescript
license: LicenseTier | undefined
```

Which BonniePDF licence applies to this application.

Set once at startup, before generating the first document:

```ts
import { settings } from '@bonniepdf/core';
settings.license = 'community';
```

There is no licence key, no activation, and no telemetry — this is a self-declaration. `BONNIEPDF_LICENSE` in the environment is an equivalent way to state it where a startup hook is awkward; this setting takes precedence over it.

Assigning a value outside [`LicenseTier`](license-tier.md) throws [`InvalidLicenseTierError`](invalid-license-tier-error.md) immediately: that is a typo in your startup code, not a licensing state.

Assignment after the first document has been generated is allowed but has no retroactive effect — the one-time notice has already been decided.
